result.topic_en: Riemann derives symmetry conditions on second derivatives of the metric coefficients at a point O in normal coordinates and expresses the squared line element near O as ds_0^2 plus a curvature term in the quantities (dx_i δx_i' - δx_i dx_i')(...), noting how these conditions change under general coordinate changes.
result.transcription:
e secunda:
$2\left\{ \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota'\iota''}}{\partial x_{\iota'''}\partial x_{\iota}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota''\iota'''}}{\partial x_{\iota}\partial x_{\iota'}} \right\} = \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota'\iota''}}{\partial x_{\iota}\partial x_{\iota'''}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'''}}{\partial x_{\iota'}\partial x_{\iota''}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota'\iota'''}}{\partial x_{\iota}\partial x_{\iota''}}$
et permutatione etc:
$2\left\{ \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota'\iota''}}{\partial x_{\iota'''}\partial x_{\iota}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'''}}{\partial x_{\iota'}\partial x_{\iota''}} \right\} = \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota''}}{\partial x_{\iota'}\partial x_{\iota'''}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota'\iota'''}}{\partial x_{\iota}\partial x_{\iota''}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota''\iota'''}}{\partial x_{\iota}\partial x_{\iota'}}$
Unde addendo et denotando per S summam omnium harum derivationum secundi ordinis
$2 S = 3\left( \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota''\iota'''}}{\partial x_{\iota}\partial x_{\iota'}} - \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}} \right)$
unde habemus; quum S non mutetur, mutatis $\iota''\iota'''$ cum $\iota\iota'$:
5.) $\frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota''\iota'''}}{\partial x_{\iota}\partial x_{\iota'}} = \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}}$
6. $\frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota''}}{\partial x_{\iota'''}\partial x_{\iota'}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'''}}{\partial x_{\iota'}\partial x_{\iota''}} = \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota''\iota'''}}{\partial x_{\iota}\partial x_{\iota'}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota'\iota'''}}{\partial x_{\iota}\partial x_{\iota''}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota'\iota''}}{\partial x_{\iota}\partial x_{\iota'''}} = 0$ in puncto O.
Nunc est quadratum elementi linearis a puncto O ducti:
$ds_0^2 = \sum_{\iota\iota'} a^0_{\iota\iota'} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'}$
a puncto $x_1 \ldots x_n$ ducti, puncto O infinite vicino:
$ds^2 = \sum_{\iota\iota'} a^0_{\iota\iota'} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'} + \sum_{\iota\iota'\iota''}\left(\frac{\partial a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}}\right)_0 x_{\iota''} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'} + \frac{1}{2}\sum_{\iota\iota'\iota''\iota'''}\left(\frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}}\right)_0 x_{\iota''}x_{\iota'''} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'}$
[-et quum in parte laeva terminus secundus evanescat.-]
[-$ds^2 = ds_0^2 + \ldots \delta\delta \sum_{\iota\iota'} a_{\iota\iota'}$ et-]
Terminus secundus in parte dextra hujus expressionis evanescit, Terminus tertius mutatis $x_\iota$ in $\delta x_\iota$, variationibus $\delta$ [?] ita determinatis ut sit $dx_\iota$ constans, ita exhiberi potest:
$dd \sum_{\iota\iota'} a_{\iota\iota'} \delta x_\iota \delta x_{\iota'} = \delta\delta \sum_{\iota\iota'} a_{\iota\iota'} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'}$
ope aequationis (5). At facile deducitur ex aequatione (6):
$dd \sum_{\iota\iota'} a_{\iota\iota'} \delta x_\iota \delta x_{\iota'} + 2\, d\delta \sum_{\iota\iota'} a_{\iota\iota'} dx_\iota \delta x_{\iota'}$
unde hic terminus fit:
$dd \sum_{\iota\iota'} a_{\iota\iota'} \delta x_\iota \delta x_{\iota'} = [-\frac{2}{3}\sum\ldots-] \frac{1}{3}\left\{ dd \sum_{\iota\iota'} a_{\iota\iota'} \delta x_\iota \delta x_{\iota'} - 2\, d\delta \sum_{\iota\iota'} a_{\iota\iota'} dx_\iota \delta x_{\iota'} + \delta\delta \sum_{\iota\iota'} a_{\iota\iota'} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'} \right\}$
Qui et ipse facile in formam redit:
$\frac{1}{3}\sum_{\iota\iota'(4)} \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}} \{ dx_\iota dx_{\iota'} \delta x_{\iota''}\delta x_{\iota'''} + \delta x_\iota \delta x_{\iota'} dx_{\iota''} dx_{\iota'''} - dx_\iota \delta x_{\iota'} \delta x_{\iota''} dx_{\iota'''} - \delta x_\iota dx_{\iota'} dx_{\iota''} \delta x_{\iota'''} )$
$= \frac{1}{3}\sum_{\iota\iota'\iota''\iota'''} \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}} (dx_\iota \delta x_{\iota''} - \delta x_\iota dx_{\iota''})(dx_{\iota'} \delta x_{\iota'''} - \delta x_{\iota'} dx_{\iota'''})$
vel $= \frac{4}{3}\sum'_{\iota\iota'',\iota'\iota'''} \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}} (dx_\iota \delta x_{\iota''} - \delta x_\iota dx_{\iota''})(dx_{\iota'} \delta x_{\iota'''} - \delta x_{\iota'} dx_{\iota'''})$
si summa ad diversa tantum paria [-...-] indicum $\iota\iota''$; $\iota'\iota'''$ extenditur.
unde.
$ds_\delta^2 = ds_0^2 + \frac{2}{3}\sum'_{\iota\iota'',\iota'\iota'''} \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}} (dx_\iota \delta x_{\iota''} - \delta x_\iota dx_{\iota''})(dx_{\iota'} \delta x_{\iota'''} - \delta x_{\iota'} dx_{\iota'''})$
Jam si loco variabilium $x_\iota$ quaelibet aliae introducerentur, conditiones hujus expressionis non erunt eaedem, neque erunt verae aequationes 5. 6. neque [-erunt-] evanescent ut hic supposuimus variationes secundi gradus $dd$, $d\delta$, $\delta\delta$; hae conditiones itaque in formam talem redigendae

methods.what: Symmetry of second derivatives of metric coefficients at O (pair-interchange symmetry)
methods.quote: $\frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota''\iota'''}}{\partial x_{\iota}\partial x_{\iota'}} = \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}}$

methods.what: Cyclic (Bianchi-type) identity of second derivatives at O
methods.quote: $\frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota''}}{\partial x_{\iota'''}\partial x_{\iota'}} + \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'''}}{\partial x_{\iota'}\partial x_{\iota''}} = \ldots = 0$

methods.what: Taylor expansion of the line element near point O
methods.quote: $ds^2 = \sum_{\iota\iota'} a^0_{\iota\iota'} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'} + \sum_{\iota\iota'\iota''}\left(\frac{\partial a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}}\right)_0 x_{\iota''} dx_\iota dx_{\iota'} + \ldots$

methods.what: Second-order term rewritten as quadratic form in bivectors (curvature form)
methods.quote: $= \frac{1}{3}\sum_{\iota\iota'\iota''\iota'''} \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}} (dx_\iota \delta x_{\iota''} - \delta x_\iota dx_{\iota''})(dx_{\iota'} \delta x_{\iota'''} - \delta x_{\iota'} dx_{\iota'''})$

methods.what: Resulting expression for line element near O with curvature term
methods.quote: $ds_\delta^2 = ds_0^2 + \frac{2}{3}\sum'_{\iota\iota'',\iota'\iota'''} \frac{\partial^2 a_{\iota\iota'}}{\partial x_{\iota''}\partial x_{\iota'''}} (dx_\iota \delta x_{\iota''} - \delta x_\iota dx_{\iota''})(dx_{\iota'} \delta x_{\iota'''} - \delta x_{\iota'} dx_{\iota'''})$

items.quote: Jam si loco variabilium $x_\iota$ quaelibet aliae introducerentur, conditiones hujus expressionis non erunt eaedem, neque erunt verae aequationes 5. 6. neque [-erunt-] evanescent ut hic supposuimus variationes secundi gradus $dd$, $d\delta$, $\delta\delta$; hae conditiones itaque in formam talem redigendae
items.english: Now if in place of the variables x_i any others were introduced, the conditions of this expression will not be the same, nor will equations 5, 6 be true, nor will the second-degree variations dd, dδ, δδ vanish as we supposed here; these conditions must therefore be brought into such a form
